title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: Pushing the Limits of KV Cache Compression
data_curation: Pretraining uses 45T multimodal tokens at a 7:1 text-to-multimodal ratio. Low-information model-generated text (outputs of weaker models, poor machine translation) is filtered as 'implicit duplication', and more recent code is added. Image-text data is re-crawled from Common Crawl and filtered by relevance, semantic de-dup and SmolVLM quality scores. Post-training gains are attributed almost entirely to data. Each task is a (problem, environment, verifier) triplet, and the model is itself trained to construct tasks, using difficulty and correctness as rewards. Tasks are re-audited from the trajectories of every RL run that uses them. General-agent environments are mocked SaaS and enterprise tools reconstructed from employee and partner usage, plus replays of submitted failure cases. Coding environments come from hard or poorly solved agent sessions (de-duplicated by trajectory) and starred GitHub repositories. Multiple agents build each one: a containerized setup, fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass checks, solution-leak removal, solver attempts, a quality and hackability inspection, and a repair loop.
curriculum: Pretraining runs from scratch with sparse attention at 64K, extends to 1M at 34T tokens, and decays the LR by cosine from 2.6e-4 to 2.6e-5 over 28T–40T tokens. DeepSeek-ViT is trained beforehand with SigLIP on 47B pairs, then autoregressively on 236B tokens. A DSpark drafter is trained on the frozen backbone after pretraining. Post-training follows the 'standard' DeepSeek-V4 paradigm: SFT, then large-scale asynchronous RL, then a final full-vocabulary on-policy distillation (OPD) stage over all domains from more than 40 heterogeneous teachers. RL is scaled across compute and scaffolds (Claude Code versions, OpenCode, Pi, DeepSeek Harness). Successive RL runs are re-initialized by merging checkpoints from different scaffolds or configurations. The Hierarchical Sparse Indexer, FP4 KV QAT and bounded-replay simulation are introduced during post-training.
method: The architecture is a 552B-backbone MoE (plus 196B Engram parameters) with 40 layers: a 20-layer causal encoder and a 20-layer decoder (CED, after YOCO), so 8B parameters are active per token in prefill and 16B in decode. CSA2 shares global KV and indexer K across layers in Full, Reindex and Reuse modes (top-k 512). The decoder's Hierarchical Sparse Indexer restricts later layers to a pool of 16,384 candidates. The main KV cache is stored in FP4 (E2M1 with an E4M3 scale per 16 channels), cutting the global KV to 890 bytes per token. Other components: Single-Pass mHC, head-wise Muon, and Sinkhorn-balanced momentum updates for embeddings. The RL algorithm is GRPO with no stated changes. Asynchronous rollouts use sample-level dispatch, concatenated routing replay, discarding of early short samples, bounded off-policy ratio and masking of stale tokens. Reasoning effort is controllable: the prompt carries 'Reasoning Effort: b' (1–100), advantages are computed within same-effort subgroups, and the length penalty is −min(C_max, k(b)·ℓ/L_norm) with k(b)=k0·exp(−(b−b_min)/τ). Agent-Team RL rewards task score plus a collaboration bonus minus the critical-path latency of the run's dependency DAG. Reward hacking is contained with AppArmor and eBPF sandboxing in DSec.
eval_metrics: Reasoning benchmarks: GPQA Diamond, HLE, internal Codeforces and MathArena Apex. Agentic benchmarks: Terminal-Bench 2.1, 3.0 and 4.0, DeepSWE v1.1, ProgramBench (Almost@1), NL2Repo, CyberGym, SEC-Bench Pro, ExploitGym, HLE with tools, AutomationBench, Agents' Last Exam, and the visual Chartography, BabyVision and ZeroBench (pass@5). Code agents run in DeepSeek Harness Minimal with a 1M context at T=1.0 and top-p 0.95. V4.1-Flash scores: GPQA 90.9, HLE 36.8, Codeforces 3471, Apex 65.6, TB2.1 90.6, DeepSWE 74.2, CyberGym 88.1, AutomationBench 54.8, ALE 31.8. Robustness is tested across 8 scaffold configurations (DeepSWE 65.5–74.2) and across effort levels 25–100 on eight reasoning benchmarks. Multi-agent tests use ProgramBench-golden (172 tasks) and FrontierSWE v2 under wall-clock deadlines. Base-model tables report MMLU-Pro 74.1, HumanEval 79.4 and held-out BPB.
key_results: With only 16B active parameters, V4.1-Flash beats DeepSeek-V4-Flash (DeepSWE 54.4→74.2, Codeforces 3289→3471) and matches or beats Opus-5 on DeepSWE (74.0), Terminal-Bench 2.1 (89.1) and AutomationBench, with a global KV cache about 1/4 of V4-Flash's and a persistent cache about 1/8. Raising effort from 25 to 100 lifts the reasoning average from 67.1 to 76.3 for about 2.5× the tokens. Agent Teams reach 30.04% vs 20.39% single-agent on ProgramBench.
evolution_note: This report refines DeepSeek-V4's CSA/HCA sparse attention, mHC and OPD recipe. It adds YOCO-style KV sharing between encoder and decoder halves, IndexCache-style cross-layer index reuse, and DeepSeek's own Engram and DSpark modules. Its explicit claim is that post-training algorithms barely matter at this stage, and that the gains come from scaling synthesized verifiable tasks, environments and scaffold diversity. It also documents agents exploiting real sandbox vulnerabilities during RL, and it makes a trained, continuous reasoning-effort knob a deployed API feature.
